response.sql: WITH circuit_counts AS (SELECT circuitId, COUNT(*) AS race_count FROM races GROUP BY circuitId), totals AS (SELECT SUM(race_count) AS total_races FROM circuit_counts), shares AS (SELECT c.circuitId, c.race_count, CAST(c.race_count AS REAL) / t.total_races AS share FROM circuit_counts c CROSS JOIN totals t), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT s.circuitId, s.race_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS excess FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share ORDER BY excess DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The average share is taken over circuits that have at least one race in the races table, so it equals 1 divided by the number of such circuits. Circuits with no races are not part of the population.
races.circuitId has no NULL values, so every race is attributed to a circuit and the total race count is the sum of the per-circuit counts.

alternatives.interpretation: The average share is taken over every circuit in the circuits table, including circuits with zero races (each of those has share 0), so the average is 1 divided by the total number of circuits.
alternatives.sql: WITH circuit_counts AS (SELECT circuitId, COUNT(*) AS race_count FROM races GROUP BY circuitId), totals AS (SELECT SUM(race_count) AS total_races FROM circuit_counts), shares AS (SELECT circuitId, race_count, CAST(race_count AS REAL) / (SELECT total_races FROM totals) AS share FROM circuit_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM circuits) AS avg_share) SELECT s.circuitId, s.race_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS excess FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share ORDER BY excess DESC LIMIT 10;
